concerns.concern: The paper excludes Joule heating because quenching is the same at 0.4 K and 5.6 K. That argument does not hold: local heating to far above T_c in poorly conducting SiO₂ would itself make the result nearly independent of bath temperature.
concerns.quote: This does not follow; bath-temperature independence is arguably what local heating predicts.

concerns.concern: The diffusion-plus-decay form used for the hot spot is not specific to non-equilibrium phonons. Heat diffusion in a thin oxide on a Si sink gives the same form, so the fitted decay length could be a purely thermal healing length. A quantitative heat-transport model of the real stack and an on-chip micro-heater control are needed.
concerns.quote: Thus r_d ≈ 0.6 µm could be a purely thermal healing length

concerns.concern: The dissipated power is itself Joule dissipation, and the distinction between 'Joule heating' and a non-equilibrium hot spot is never defined physically. The analogy to SNSPD hot spots is asserted rather than demonstrated.
concerns.quote: is semantic until defined physically, e.g. thermalised local temperature versus a non-thermal phonon distribution.

concerns.concern: The authors' own hot-spot model predicts that the critical density and relaxation time change strongly near T_c. Yet the fitted r₀(P) and P_d are identical at 0.4 K and 5.6 K, and this is unexplained.
concerns.quote: Both thermal and critical-density models would then predict a larger r₀ at fixed P, yet the fitted r₀(P) and P_d are identical.

concerns.concern: The film's T_c, λ(T) and Pearl length are not reported in the main text. The claim that measurements span 'above the critical temperature' is confusing, since Meissner screening is imaged at 5.6–5.8 K.
concerns.quote: T_c(B₀) of the D3 film is not given in the main text.

concerns.concern: The experiment runs at µW powers, orders of magnitude above those that switch nanowires in transport gate-controlled supercurrent. The result may just show the generic fact that local dissipation destroys superconductivity, not the GCS effect itself.
concerns.quote: This is 3–6 orders of magnitude above the powers that switch nanowires in transport GCS

concerns.concern: Drift and fluctuating onset voltages of the leakage suggest the device may be operating in a regime near oxide degradation or breakdown.
concerns.quote: The leakage shows vSILC-like drift and fluctuating onset voltages V_G^ON (7–16 V), possibly indicating oxide degradation or filament formation

concerns.concern: The link to transport devices is never shown. No transport critical-current suppression is measured and correlated with the imaged suppression on the same device or film, and the nanowire-mimicking device D1 appears only in the Supplement.
concerns.quote: No transport critical-current suppression I_c(V_G, P) is correlated with imaged suppression on the same device or film.

concerns.concern: Calling GCS a 'genuine feature of superconductivity not restricted to transport' adds little, because switching to the normal state already implies loss of Meissner screening. The title and abstract wording should be revised accordingly.
concerns.quote: therefore adds less than suggested. The real novelty is the spatial map.

concerns.concern: The diffusion model uses an isotropic 3D Green's function for an infinite homogeneous medium. The real device is a strongly layered Nb/Ti/SiO₂/Si stack with 2D in-film diffusion, ballistic phonons in Si and interface boundaries.
concerns.quote: Eqs. (1)–(2) use the isotropic 3D Green's function for an infinite homogeneous medium. The real system is strongly layered

concerns.concern: The two-parameter Lambert-W fit to about 20 points over one decade of power cannot distinguish the model from other functional forms. No residuals, χ², information criteria or parameter correlations are reported.
concerns.quote: No residuals, χ², AIC/BIC or parameter correlations are given, so "excellent agreement" does not validate the microscopic picture.

concerns.concern: The model predicts suppression at any nonzero power, but the low-power regime is not tested for a threshold like those seen in transport GCS.
concerns.quote: The Lambert-W form predicts r₀ > 0 for any P > 0. This is not tested at low P

concerns.concern: The simulations use a sharp circular normal region. A diffusive quasiparticle or phonon density would instead give a graded superfluid density with similar stray fields, so the claim of 'complete suppression' beyond 1 µm is not supported.
concerns.quote: The extracted r₀ may therefore correspond to a contour of partially enhanced λ(r), or to a detection threshold, rather than to the normal-state boundary

concerns.concern: With a Pearl length (~5.8 µm) larger than the 3 µm islands, screening is weak and field features are smeared. The extraction of r₀ from the field maps is therefore only approximate.
concerns.quote: The statement that "the stray field maxima roughly delineate the superconducting region" is only approximate here.

concerns.concern: The sub-100 nm error bars on r₀ depend on assumed λ, NV height, NV orientation and reconstruction artefacts. Changes of λ with temperature are not accounted for, and systematic uncertainties are not quantified.
concerns.quote: Sub-100 nm r₀ error bars (~0.1 µm, Fig. 3a) depend on assumed λ, z₀, NV orientation, and artefacts of the Fourier vector reconstruction near edges.

concerns.concern: The two methods for extracting r₀, line-cut fitting and the B_x edge-shift method, are never applied to the same dataset to cross-validate them.
concerns.quote: The line-cut fit (which ignores vortices) and the B_x edge-shift method are never applied to a common dataset.

concerns.concern: The main quantitative device shows incomplete screening from vortices and non-superconducting grains. Vortex rearrangement between maps, tip drift and height changes can corrupt the reference subtraction.
concerns.quote: Vortices invalidate the first method for part of the data, and their impact on the second method is not shown.

concerns.concern: The leakage current path and the location of dissipation are assumed to be at the gate apex rather than demonstrated. The current could flow through the surface, bulk oxide, the Si or evolving filaments, any of which could move the hot spot.
concerns.quote: The interpretation rests on a point-like source at the gate apex. Yet the nature and stability of the current path are not determined

concerns.concern: Parasitic 60 GΩ wiring leakage contributes to the measured current. The fraction of power actually dissipated near the device is not quantified, which matters most at low power.
concerns.quote: The 60 GΩ parasitic wiring/connector leakage contributes to the measured I_L, at least at lower V_G.

concerns.concern: Excluding a direct electric-field effect is nearly trivial, because fields are screened within nanometres in a metal. It therefore says little about the nanoconstrictions where the field effect was proposed.
concerns.quote: Suppression over >1 µm cannot be a direct field effect almost by construction

concerns.concern: The claimed weak correlation between r₀ and gate voltage is misleading. Within each cool-down subset r₀ is steep and monotonic in |V_G|, and the apparent weakness comes from offsets due to onset-voltage drift.
concerns.quote: The apparent weak correlation arises mainly from the offset between subsets caused by V_G^ON drift.

concerns.concern: Polarity independence does not discriminate between mechanisms. Reversing polarity moves the dissipation site only ~80 nm, below resolution, and any dissipation-driven mechanism, including Joule heating, would also be polarity independent.
concerns.quote: It therefore cannot discriminate NEPs from heating or from injection-type mechanisms.

concerns.concern: The quasiparticle lifetime estimate uses a diffusion coefficient taken from a different material and a room-temperature thermal diffusivity of glass. Neither is appropriate for this sub-Kelvin Nb/Ti/SiO₂ system.
concerns.quote: The substrate estimate (τ ≈ 350 ns) uses room-temperature thermal diffusivity of glass (Ref. 29).

concerns.concern: Dismissing the substrate-diffusion scenario as 'unreasonably long' is unjustified. The lifetime therefore spans more than two orders of magnitude and should not be quoted in the abstract as τ ~ 10⁻⁹ s.
concerns.quote: τ spans more than two orders of magnitude (~0.7–350 ns) and carries little microscopic information.

concerns.concern: In-film quasiparticle diffusion is hard to reconcile with quenching of a floating island whose source sits about 0.8 µm away.
concerns.quote: In-film quasiparticle diffusion is hard to reconcile with quenching when the island is floating and the source sits ~0.8 µm away

concerns.concern: An energy-budget check is missing: the implied critical energy density should be compared with the Nb condensation energy density. This check does not obviously favour the authors' preferred scenario.
concerns.quote: Notably, this comparison does not obviously favour the scenario the authors consider "reasonable."

concerns.concern: The fitted parameters are not used to make quantitative, parameter-free predictions for the floating-island and extended-gate configurations. These are compared only qualitatively.
concerns.quote: The reduced suppression in the floating-island G4–G5 configuration is described only as "consistent with" a source displaced by ~0.8 µm.

concerns.concern: The characteristic power P_d differs by a factor of about 3 between devices while the decay length is similar. This unexplained difference implies large variations in injection efficiency or critical density.
concerns.quote: P_d differs by a factor ~2.6–3 between D2b (0.36 µW) and D3 (0.95 µW), while r_d is similar.

concerns.concern: The normal ~5 nm Ti adhesion layer acts as a proximity layer and quasiparticle trap that likely affects λ and the critical density, but it is ignored.
concerns.quote: It acts as a proximity layer and quasiparticle trap, likely affecting both λ and ρ_c, but it is ignored.

concerns.concern: The NV laser illumination and microwave pulses could generate quasiparticles or heating and alter the suppression or vortex configuration. Their powers and duty cycles are not reported or controlled for.
concerns.quote: Laser and microwave powers and duty cycles are not reported.

concerns.concern: It is not reported whether the suppression is reversible or hysteretic when power is cycled, or how quickly it sets in during a scan.
concerns.quote: It is unclear whether r₀ is reversible when P is swept up and down

concerns.concern: The power drifts and fluctuates during long scans under constant-current operation. It is unclear how the quoted power relates to the instantaneous suppression, and horizontal error bars on P are missing.
concerns.quote: Under constant-current operation with drifting V_G (Fig. S2), P drifts during a scan.

concerns.concern: The vortex-expulsion observation rests on a few maps, yet it is emphasised in the abstract. It lacks cooling history, reversibility, statistics and alternative explanations, and the non-monotonic temperature dependence of the escape power is unexplained.
concerns.quote: The claim rests on a few maps. The escape power is non-monotonic in temperature

concerns.concern: Novelty relative to prior transport work is overstated. Remote-gate, floating-island and leakage- or phonon-mediated suppression were already demonstrated, so the imaging itself should be framed as the main advance.
concerns.quote: The manuscript's main conceptual conclusion therefore largely confirms existing interpretations

concerns.concern: The dimensionality and units of ρ in Eq. (1) should be stated explicitly, given the thin-film geometry.
concerns.quote: its dimensionality and the units of ρ should be stated explicitly in the text

concerns.concern: Reference 13 has a mismatched year and DOI.
concerns.quote: The year/DOI in Ref. 13 do not match and should be corrected.
